title: Session Stitching with 30-Minute Gap Tolerance
description:
An `events` table records user activity timestamps. Two consecutive events for the same user belong to the **same session** if the gap between them is ≤ 30 minutes; a gap of more than 30 minutes starts a new session.

For each user, identify all sessions and compute: session start time, session end time, number of events, and session duration in minutes.

**Table: events**

| Column | Type |
|--------|------|
| event_id | INT |
| user_id | INT |
| event_time | TIMESTAMP |
| event_type | VARCHAR |

Output columns: `user_id`, `session_num`, `session_start`, `session_end`, `event_count`, `duration_minutes`. Order by `user_id`, `session_num`.
solution_sql: WITH event_gaps AS (SELECT event_id, user_id, event_time, event_type, LAG(event_time) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY event_time) AS prev_time FROM events), session_flags AS (SELECT *, CASE WHEN prev_time IS NULL OR EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (event_time - prev_time)) > 1800 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS new_session FROM event_gaps), session_ids AS (SELECT *, SUM(new_session) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY event_time ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS session_num FROM session_flags) SELECT user_id, session_num, MIN(event_time) AS session_start, MAX(event_time) AS session_end, COUNT(*) AS event_count, ROUND(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM MAX(event_time) - MIN(event_time)) / 60.0, 1) AS duration_minutes FROM session_ids GROUP BY user_id, session_num ORDER BY user_id, session_num

test_cases.description: Sessions per user with correct start/end times and event counts

hints: Use LAG() to compare each event's timestamp with the previous event for the same user. Flag a new session (1) when the gap exceeds 1800 seconds (30 minutes) or when there is no previous event.
Apply a cumulative SUM() of the session-start flag ordered by event_time within each user partition. This creates a session identifier that increments each time a new session begins.
explanation: This problem requires a three-step CTE chain. First, LAG() computes the time since the previous event per user. Second, a CASE expression flags each event as a session starter (gap > 30 min or first event). Third, a cumulative SUM() of those flags — partitioned by user and ordered by time — assigns a monotonically increasing session ID. Finally, GROUP BY user_id and session_num aggregates session metrics. The EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM ...) / 60 trick converts a timestamp interval to minutes. This session-stitching pattern is fundamental to product analytics at every consumer tech company.
